//: Composite indexes for the Clarity 360 response collection.
GET /school-climate/sessions fetched EVERY document in `responses` and
filtered dates in memory, with a comment saying it did so to avoid needing a
composite index. That works at test scale and degrades forever: Firestore
bills per document read, so each dashboard refresh costs one read per answer
ever recorded, and the latency grows linearly with the product's success.
These indexes let the same queries run server-side. Deploy with:
These index the ts_at Timestamp rather than the ts string. That is only safe
because backfill-ts-at.mjs has already run: 4393 of 4393 documents carry the
field, 0 unparseable. The ordering mattered -- Firestore OMITS documents that
lack an indexed field, so indexing ts_at first would have silently dropped
every historical document from date-filtered results, with no error anywhere.
`ts` is still written and remains the human-readable value in exports. If a
future field is added to these documents, backfill it before indexing it.
